question: In the mid-eighth century, Dantidurga, a Rashtrakuta chief, overthrew his Chalukya overlord and performed a ritual literally called a ______ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is Golden womb.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the mid-eighth century CE, Dantidurga, a Rashtrakuta chief, overthrew his Chalukya overlord (Kirtivarman II) and performed the ritual called Hiranya-garbha, which literally means the “golden womb”. (हिरण्यगर्भ — स्वर्ण गर्भ)

• The ritual was believed to lead to the “rebirth” of the sacrificer as a Kshatriya, even if he was not one by birth — a way of legitimising newly won kingship.

• Dantidurga founded the Rashtrakuta dynasty with its capital at Manyakheta (Malkhed) in present-day Karnataka.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Prayer meet is not a royal legitimising ritual of early medieval India.

• Horse ride loosely hints at the Ashvamedha (horse sacrifice), a different ritual performed to assert paramount sovereignty.

• Subsidiary Alliance was a 19th-century policy of Lord Wellesley (1798), not an eighth-century ritual.

NOTE

• Other legitimising rituals: Rajasuya (royal consecration) and Vajapeya.

• Famous Rashtrakuta achievement: the rock-cut Kailasanatha temple at Ellora, built under Krishna I.

question: Who was the first Indian actress to receive the Padma Shri Award?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nargis Dutt.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Nargis Dutt (born Fatima Rashid) was the first Indian actress to be awarded the Padma Shri, in 1958. (पद्म श्री — चौथा सर्वोच्च नागरिक सम्मान)

• She is best remembered for Mother India (1957), for which she won the Filmfare Best Actress Award.

• She later became a nominated member of the Rajya Sabha; the Nargis Dutt Award for Best Feature Film on National Integration is named after her.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Asha Parekh received the Padma Shri in 1992 and the Dadasaheb Phalke Award in 2020 (conferred in 2022).

• Madhubala, star of *Mughal-e-Azam*, never received a Padma award.

• Devika Rani, the “First Lady of Indian Cinema”, was the first recipient of the Dadasaheb Phalke Award (1969) and received the Padma Shri in 1958 as well, but Nargis is credited as the first actress so honoured.

NOTE

• Order of civilian awards: Bharat Ratna > Padma Vibhushan > Padma Bhushan > Padma Shri.

• Padma awards were instituted in 1954 and are announced on Republic Day.

question: The percentage of eligible voters who cast their votes in an election is termed as ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Turnout.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Voter turnout is the percentage of eligible (registered) voters who actually cast their votes in an election. (मतदान प्रतिशत)

• High turnout is treated as an indicator of popular participation and faith in the democratic process; India’s 2019 Lok Sabha turnout was a record 67.4%.

• The Election Commission of India (Article 324) runs the SVEEP programme to raise turnout.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Quorum — the minimum number of members required to be present to conduct business; in Parliament it is one-tenth of the total membership of the House (Article 100).

• Veto — the power to reject a proposal or bill; the President of India enjoys absolute, suspensive and pocket veto.

• Constituency — a territorial area whose voters elect one representative.

NOTE

• National Voters’ Day is observed on 25 January, marking the ECI’s foundation in 1950.

• Voting age was lowered from 21 to 18 years by the 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988.

question: Who was the last tirthankara of the Jainas?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vardhamana Mahavira.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Vardhamana Mahavira was the 24th and last Tirthankara of Jainism. (तीर्थंकर — जैन धर्म के उपदेशक)

• He was born at Kundagrama (Vaishali, Bihar) in 599 BCE and attained nirvana at Pavapuri in 527 BCE; his symbol is the lion.

• He preached the Triratna (right faith, right knowledge, right conduct) and five vows: ahimsa, satya, asteya, aparigraha and brahmacharya (the fifth added by him).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Rishabhanatha (Adinatha) was the first Tirthankara; his symbol is the bull, and he is mentioned in the Rig Veda.

• Chandraprabha was the 8th Tirthankara (symbol: crescent moon).

• Padmaprabha was the 6th Tirthankara (symbol: red lotus).

NOTE

• Parshvanatha, the 23rd Tirthankara, preached four vows and is symbolised by the snake.

• Jainism split into Digambara and Svetambara sects; sacred texts are the Agamas, written in Ardhamagadhi Prakrit.

question: As of 11 August 2022, who is the Chairman of Rajya Sabha?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jagdeep Dhankhar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under Article 64, the Vice-President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. (राज्यसभा के सभापति)

• Jagdeep Dhankhar took oath as the 14th Vice-President of India on 11 August 2022, defeating Margaret Alva, and thereby became Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

• He was earlier the Governor of West Bengal (2019–2022).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Adhir Ranjan Chowdhury was the leader of the Congress party in the Lok Sabha at that time.

• Narendra Modi is the Prime Minister of India (since 2014).

• Amit Shah is the Union Home Minister and also handles the Ministry of Cooperation.

NOTE

• The Vice-President is elected by an electoral college of both Houses of Parliament (elected + nominated members) by proportional representation through single transferable vote — Article 66.

• Minimum age for the Vice-President is 35 years; term is 5 years.

question: Which among the following is an example of Phylum Mammalia of Animal Kingdom?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The rat is a mammal — it is warm-blooded, has hair/fur, mammary glands that produce milk, and gives birth to live young (viviparous). (स्तनपायी)

• Mammalia is actually a class within the phylum Chordata; other mammalian features are a four-chambered heart, diaphragm and external ear (pinna).

• Rats belong to the order Rodentia, characterised by continuously growing incisors.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Crocodile belongs to class Reptilia — cold-blooded, scaly skin, lays eggs.

• Hen and Pigeon belong to class Aves — feathers, beak, hollow (pneumatic) bones, oviparous.

• Only mammals possess sweat glands and hair as defining features.

NOTE

• Egg-laying mammals: Platypus and Echidna (order Monotremata).

• Whale, dolphin and bat are mammals though they swim/fly; bat is the only mammal capable of true flight.

• The Blue Whale is the largest mammal on earth.

question: Which Department of Government of India launched ‘One Health’ pilot project in April 2022?
option_1: Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying
solution_text:
The correct answer is Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In April 2022, the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD), under the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, launched the ‘One Health’ pilot project in Karnataka and Uttarakhand. (वन हेल्थ — एक स्वास्थ्य)

• The One Health approach recognises that human, animal and environmental health are interlinked, and aims at coordinated surveillance and control of zoonotic diseases.

• It was implemented with support from the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation and the Indian Council of Medical Research ecosystem partners.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Department of Consumer Affairs handles consumer protection, weights and measures, and the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.

• The IT sector is handled by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY).

• Department of Commerce deals with foreign trade, EXIM policy and trade agreements.

NOTE

• Other DAHD initiatives: Rashtriya Gokul Mission, National Livestock Mission, National Animal Disease Control Programme (NADCP) for FMD and Brucellosis.

• Examples of zoonotic diseases: rabies, anthrax, brucellosis, avian influenza, COVID-19.

question: Indian constitution borrowed cabinet form of governance from __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is United Kingdom.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India borrowed the cabinet (parliamentary) form of government from the United Kingdom. (संसदीय शासन प्रणाली)

• Other features taken from the UK: rule of law, single citizenship, bicameral legislature, Speaker’s office, writs, legislative procedure and the Prime Minister’s office.

• Under this system the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha (Article 75).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• France — the ideals of Liberty, Equality and Fraternity and the concept of a Republic.

• South Africa — the procedure for amendment of the Constitution and the election of Rajya Sabha members.

• Australia — the Concurrent List, freedom of trade and commerce, and the joint sitting of Parliament.

NOTE

• USA — Fundamental Rights, judicial review, independence of judiciary, impeachment of the President, post of Vice-President.

• Ireland — Directive Principles, nomination to Rajya Sabha, method of election of the President.

• Canada — federation with a strong Centre, residuary powers with the Centre.

question: Which of the following is not an environment function?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Accumulates waste.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The four recognised functions of the environment are: supplying resources, sustaining life, assimilating (absorbing) waste, and enhancing the quality of life. (पर्यावरण के कार्य)

• The environment assimilates or absorbs waste — it does not accumulate it. Accumulation of waste happens only when the waste load exceeds the environment’s carrying capacity, causing pollution.

• Hence “Accumulates waste” is not an environmental function but a symptom of environmental degradation.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Sustains life — the environment provides the “Sun, soil, water and air” essential for life.

• Provides the supply of resources — both renewable (trees, water) and non-renewable (fossil fuels, minerals).

• Enhances quality of life — through scenic beauty, rivers, oceans and recreation.

NOTE

• Environmental crisis arises when the rate of resource extraction exceeds the rate of regeneration.

• World Environment Day — 5 June; Earth Day — 22 April.

question: Which of the following crop is known as "Golden Fibre" of Bengal?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jute.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Jute is called the “Golden Fibre” because of its golden-brown shine and its high commercial value in Bengal. (जूट — सुनहरा रेशा)

• It grows best in well-drained alluvial soil of flood plains with high temperature (25–35°C) and heavy rainfall; it needs the Ganga–Brahmaputra delta conditions.

• West Bengal is the largest producer of jute in India, followed by Bihar and Assam.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Soyabean is an oilseed and pulse crop; Madhya Pradesh is the leading producer.

• Corn (maize) is a kharif food-cum-fodder crop; Karnataka and Madhya Pradesh are major producers.

• Rice is India’s principal food crop; West Bengal is the largest producer.

NOTE

• Other nicknames: Cotton — White Gold, Tea — Black Gold (also crude oil), Turmeric — Golden Spice.

• The National Jute Board functions under the Ministry of Textiles; India’s first jute mill was set up at Rishra (1855) near Kolkata.

question: Meena talks about an example of sedimentary rock. Which one of the following can it be?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sandstone.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sandstone is a sedimentary rock formed by the compaction and cementation of sand-sized grains deposited by water or wind. (अवसादी चट्टान)

• Sedimentary rocks are stratified (layered) and often contain fossils — they are the only rock type where fossils are commonly found.

• The Red Fort and Fatehpur Sikri are built of red sandstone quarried in Rajasthan.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Granite is an igneous (intrusive/plutonic) rock, coarse-grained, formed by slow cooling of magma below the surface.

• Marble is a metamorphic rock formed from limestone; the Taj Mahal is built of white marble.

• Basalt is an igneous (extrusive/volcanic) rock; the Deccan Trap is made of basalt, which weathers into fertile black (regur) soil.

NOTE

• Metamorphic pairs: Limestone → Marble, Sandstone → Quartzite, Clay → Slate, Coal → Graphite/Diamond, Granite → Gneiss.

• Other sedimentary rocks: shale, limestone, conglomerate, coal, gypsum.

question: Pongal, the four day Harvest festival is generally celebrated in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is South India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pongal is a four-day harvest festival celebrated mainly in Tamil Nadu (South India) in the Tamil month of Thai (mid-January). (पोंगल — फसल कटाई का त्योहार)

• Its four days are Bhogi Pongal, Surya (Thai) Pongal, Mattu Pongal and Kaanum Pongal; it is dedicated to the Sun God.

• It coincides with Makar Sankranti and marks the beginning of Uttarayana, the sun’s northward journey.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• North-East India — harvest festivals are Bihu (Assam), Wangala (Meghalaya) and Ka Pomblang Nongkrem.

• North India — Lohri (Punjab) and Baisakhi are the harvest festivals.

• Eastern India — Nuakhai (Odisha) and Poush Parbon (West Bengal).

NOTE

• Other harvest festivals: Onam (Kerala), Ugadi/Gudi Padwa, Makar Sankranti (Gujarat/Maharashtra), Bhogali Bihu (Assam).

• Jallikattu, the bull-taming sport, is held during Mattu Pongal in Tamil Nadu.

question: Who wrote the Panchatantra, a collection of fables?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vishnu Sharma.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Panchatantra, a celebrated collection of animal fables in Sanskrit, was composed by Vishnu Sharma. (पंचतंत्र — विष्णु शर्मा)

• It was written to teach niti (statecraft and worldly wisdom) to the dull sons of a king, and is divided into five books (tantras): *Mitra-bheda, Mitra-labha, Kakolukiyam, Labdhapranasam* and *Aparikshitakarakam*.

• It is one of the most widely translated works of Indian literature, rendered into Persian as *Kalila wa Dimna*.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Rumi was a 13th-century Persian Sufi poet and mystic, author of the *Masnavi*.

• Jayadeva was a 12th-century Sanskrit poet in the court of Lakshmana Sena of Bengal, famous for the Gita Govinda.

• Amar Singh is associated with the Sanskrit lexicon Amarakosha (by Amarasimha, a scholar in Chandragupta II’s court).

NOTE

• Related fable collection: the Hitopadesha by Narayan Pandit.

• Other Sanskrit classics: Abhijnanashakuntalam, Meghadutam, Raghuvamsha — Kalidasa; Mudrarakshasa — Vishakhadatta; Mrichchhakatika — Shudraka.

question: Who defeated Prithviraj Chauhan in the second battle of Tarain in 1192 AD?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Muhammad Ghori.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Second Battle of Tarain (1192 AD) was fought between Muhammad Ghori and Prithviraj Chauhan III, in which Ghori defeated and killed Prithviraj. (तराईन का द्वितीय युद्ध)

• In the First Battle of Tarain (1191 AD), Prithviraj Chauhan had defeated Muhammad Ghori.

• The victory of 1192 laid the foundation of Muslim rule in North India; Ghori’s slave Qutb-ud-din Aibak founded the Slave (Mamluk) Dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate in 1206.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Iltutmish (1211–1236) was the real consolidator of the Delhi Sultanate; he introduced the Iqta system and the coins tanka (silver) and jital (copper).

• Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi in the First Battle of Panipat (1526), founding the Mughal Empire.

• Alauddin Khilji (1296–1316) is known for market (price) control reforms and his general Malik Kafur’s Deccan campaigns.

NOTE

• Battle of Chandawar (1194) — Muhammad Ghori defeated Jaichand of Kannauj.

• Prithviraj Raso, written by Chand Bardai, is a poetic account of Prithviraj Chauhan’s life.

question: Tata Iron and steel company (TISCO) began producing steel in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1912.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• TISCO (Tata Iron and Steel Company) was set up by Jamsetji Nusserwanji Tata and registered in Bombay in 1907; it began producing steel in 1912. (टाटा आयरन एंड स्टील कंपनी)

• The plant was located at Sakchi, near the confluence of the Subarnarekha and Kharkai rivers in present-day Jamshedpur, Jharkhand.

• The site was chosen for its proximity to iron ore, coal and manganese deposits and to the Kolkata–Nagpur railway line.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• 1914–1918 — the First World War, during which TISCO supplied rails and shells to the British, expanding rapidly.

• 1907 is the year of TISCO’s incorporation, not of steel production.

• Sakchi was renamed Jamshedpur in 1919 by Lord Chelmsford, in honour of Jamsetji Tata.

NOTE

• India’s first iron and steel plant attempt: Bengal Iron Works, Kulti (1870).

• Other major steel plants: Bhilai and Bokaro (USSR help), Rourkela (Germany), Durgapur (UK).

question: Which among the following is a folk dance of Jammu and Kashmir, India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rouf.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rouf (Ruf/Rov) is a folk dance of Jammu and Kashmir, performed mainly by women in rows facing each other, especially during Ramzan, Eid and the spring season. (रौफ — जम्मू-कश्मीर का लोक नृत्य)

• Other folk dances of Jammu and Kashmir: Kud, Dumhal, Bhand Pather, Hafiza, Bacha Nagma and Chakri.

• Dumhal is performed by the men of the Wattal tribe, wearing tall conical caps.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Kathak is a classical dance of Uttar Pradesh, known for its *tatkar* (footwork) and *chakkars* (spins).

• Bihu is the folk dance of Assam, associated with the Bihu festival.

• Bhangra is the energetic harvest folk dance of Punjab, performed to the dhol during Baisakhi.

NOTE

• The eight classical dances of India: Bharatanatyam (TN), Kathak (UP), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (AP), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur), Sattriya (Assam).

• Chhau (Jharkhand/Odisha/West Bengal) is a UNESCO-listed martial folk dance.

question: Which sport is played between two teams each made up of eleven players?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cricket.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Cricket is played between two teams of eleven players each. (क्रिकेट — ग्यारह खिलाड़ी)

• It is played on an oval field with a 22-yard pitch in the centre; the governing body is the International Cricket Council (ICC), headquartered at Dubai.

• India’s cricket board is the BCCI (1928); famous cricket terms include googly, LBW, silly point, maiden over and hat-trick.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Swimming is an individual sport (though relays have 4 members per team).

• Basketball has five players per side on court; governing body FIBA.

• Table tennis is played as singles (1 v 1) or doubles (2 v 2); governing body ITTF.

NOTE

• Other 11-player team sports: Football and Hockey.

• Players per side: Kabaddi – 7, Volleyball – 6, Basketball – 5, Polo – 4, Water polo – 7, Baseball – 9.

question: The Indian classical dancer Sonal Mansingh was honoured with which of the following awards?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Padma Bhushan and Padma Vibhushan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sonal Mansingh is an eminent Indian classical dancer of Bharatanatyam and Odissi. (सोनल मानसिंह)

• She was awarded the Padma Bhushan in 1992 and the Padma Vibhushan in 2003, becoming the first woman dancer to receive the Padma Vibhushan.

• She also received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1987) and was nominated to the Rajya Sabha in 2018.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Bharat Ratna is India’s highest civilian award; among performing artists it has gone to M. S. Subbulakshmi, Ravi Shankar, Bhimsen Joshi and Lata Mangeshkar — not to Sonal Mansingh.

• She founded the Centre for Indian Classical Dances (CICD) in New Delhi in 1977.

• Other famous Odissi exponents: Kelucharan Mohapatra, Sanjukta Panigrahi, Madhavi Mudgal.

NOTE

• Famous Bharatanatyam dancers: Rukmini Devi Arundale, Balasaraswati, Yamini Krishnamurthy, Padma Subrahmanyam.

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi (1953) is India’s national academy for music, dance and drama.

question: Which river of India drains into Bay of Bengal?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Godavari.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Godavari rises at Trimbakeshwar in Nashik district, Maharashtra, and flows eastwards to drain into the Bay of Bengal. (गोदावरी — दक्षिण गंगा)

• It is the largest peninsular river of India and is called the “Dakshin Ganga” (Ganga of the South); length about 1,465 km.

• Its main tributaries are the Purna, Pravara, Manjra, Penganga, Wardha, Wainganga, Indravati and Sabari.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Tapi (Tapti) flows westwards through a rift valley and falls into the Gulf of Khambhat (Arabian Sea).

• Narmada also flows westwards through a rift valley between the Vindhyas and Satpuras into the Gulf of Khambhat; it forms the Dhuadhar Falls at Bhedaghat.

• Mahi rises in Madhya Pradesh, crosses the Tropic of Cancer twice, and drains into the Arabian Sea.

NOTE

• Peninsular rivers draining into the Bay of Bengal: Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri, Subarnarekha, Penna.

• Rivers draining into the Arabian Sea: Narmada, Tapi, Sabarmati, Mahi, Periyar, Luni.

question: GDP is an indicator of a country's economy. What does 'D' in GDP stand for?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Domestic.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• GDP stands for Gross Domestic Product — so ‘D’ stands for Domestic. (सकल घरेलू उत्पाद)

• GDP is the total money value of all final goods and services produced within the domestic territory of a country during a financial year.

• In India, GDP estimates are prepared by the National Statistical Office (NSO) under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI); the current base year is 2011–12.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• GNP = GDP + Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA).

• NDP = GDP − Depreciation; NNP = GNP − Depreciation.

• NNP at factor cost is also called National Income; Per capita income = National Income ÷ Population.

NOTE

• Nominal GDP is at current prices; Real GDP is at constant (base-year) prices — real GDP is the better measure of growth.

• GDP Deflator = (Nominal GDP / Real GDP) × 100.

• The concept of GDP was developed by Simon Kuznets.

question: In cricket, hitting the ball to the boundary along the ground is __________ runs.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 4.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In cricket, when the batter hits the ball and it reaches or crosses the boundary along the ground (after bouncing or rolling), the batting side is awarded four runs. (चौका — 4 रन)

• If the ball crosses the boundary without touching the ground (i.e., on the full), six runs are awarded.

• Runs are added to the batter’s score, and the batters do not need to complete any physical runs.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• 1 and 2 runs are scored by the batters physically running between the wickets.

• A boundary 4 is popularly called a “four” or chauka, and a boundary 6 is a “six” or chhakka.

• Overthrows that reach the boundary add 4 runs to the runs already completed.

NOTE

• Cricket extras: wide, no-ball, bye and leg-bye; a wide or no-ball gives 1 run plus a re-bowled delivery.

• The ICC governs world cricket; important trophies: World Cup, Champions Trophy, Ashes, Ranji Trophy, Duleep Trophy, Irani Trophy, Deodhar Trophy.

question: The census of India is conducted at an interval of ________ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is 10 years.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Census of India is conducted once every ten years (decennial). (जनगणना — प्रत्येक दस वर्ष)

• It is carried out by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India, under the Ministry of Home Affairs, as per the Census Act, 1948.

• The first complete census was held in 1881 under Lord Ripon; the first non-synchronous attempt was in 1872 under Lord Mayo.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Census 2011 was the 15th National Census and the 7th after Independence; its motto was “Our Census, Our Future”.

• Census 2011 figures: population 121.09 crore; sex ratio 943; literacy 74.04%; density 382 persons/sq km.

• Most populous state — Uttar Pradesh; least populous — Sikkim; highest literacy — Kerala; highest sex ratio — Kerala (1084).

NOTE

• Population is a Union List subject (Entry 69 of List I).

• Lowest density — Arunachal Pradesh (17); highest density — Bihar (1106) among states, Delhi among UTs.

question: The rock – cave temple of ______ is the largest monolithic structure in the world.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ellora.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Kailasa (Kailasanatha) temple at Ellora, Cave 16, is the largest monolithic rock-cut structure in the world, carved out of a single rock from top to bottom. (एलोरा — एकाश्म संरचना)

• It was built in the 8th century CE under the Rashtrakuta ruler Krishna I and is dedicated to Lord Shiva.

• The Ellora caves (34 caves) in Aurangabad (Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar), Maharashtra, contain Buddhist, Hindu and Jain caves together and are a UNESCO World Heritage Site (1983).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Ajanta caves (Maharashtra) are 30 Buddhist caves famous for mural paintings and the fresco technique; UNESCO site since 1983.

• Udayagiri caves are located in Madhya Pradesh (Gupta period, Vidisha) and in Odisha (Jain caves of Kharavela at Udayagiri–Khandagiri).

• Badami caves in Karnataka were built by the Chalukyas of Badami (6th century).

NOTE

• Ellora caves 1–12 — Buddhist; 13–29 — Hindu; 30–34 — Jain.

• Ajanta and Ellora were both patronised over centuries; Ajanta paintings depict the Jataka tales.

question: Lala Lajpat Rai was an active member of which organisation?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Arya Samaj.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Lala Lajpat Rai, known as “Punjab Kesari” or the Lion of Punjab, was an active member and leader of the Arya Samaj. (आर्य समाज)

• The Arya Samaj was founded by Swami Dayanand Saraswati in 1875 at Bombay, with the slogan “Back to the Vedas”; his famous work is Satyarth Prakash.

• Lajpat Rai was part of the extremist trio “Lal–Bal–Pal”, founded the Punjab National Bank and Lakshmi Insurance Company, and died in 1928 of injuries received during a lathi charge while protesting the Simon Commission.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Brahmo Sabha was founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in 1828; it was later renamed the Brahmo Samaj.

• Brahmo Samaj was led by Debendranath Tagore and Keshab Chandra Sen, and worked against sati, idolatry and caste.

• Prarthana Samaj was founded in 1867 at Bombay by Atmaram Pandurang, with M. G. Ranade as its leading light.

NOTE

• Other reform bodies: Satyashodhak Samaj (Jyotiba Phule, 1873), Ramakrishna Mission (Swami Vivekananda, 1897), Theosophical Society (1875).

• Lala Lajpat Rai founded the Servants of the People Society (1921).

question: What is the chemical name for ionic compound MgCl₂?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Magnesium chloride.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In MgCl₂, Mg is the symbol of magnesium and Cl of chlorine, so the compound is magnesium chloride. (मैग्नीशियम क्लोराइड)

• It is an ionic (electrovalent) compound: magnesium loses 2 electrons to form Mg²⁺ and each chlorine gains 1 electron to form Cl⁻, hence the formula MgCl₂.

• Ionic compounds are generally solid, brittle, have high melting points, and conduct electricity in molten or aqueous state.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Sodium iodide is NaI.

• Manganese chloride is MnCl₂ — note that manganese is Mn, not Mg.

• Cesium fluoride is CsF.

NOTE

• Common formulae: NaCl – common salt, CaO – quicklime, Ca(OH)₂ – slaked lime, NaHCO₃ – baking soda, Na₂CO₃·10H₂O – washing soda, CaOCl₂ – bleaching powder.

• Magnesium burns with a dazzling white light and is a constituent of chlorophyll; MgSO₄·7H₂O is Epsom salt.
